The words-only model is noise of order +-5-10% with NO consistent sign - Ep. 06 +10.4%, Ep. 07 -0.4%, Ep. 08 -5.0%, Ep. 09 +2.7%, Ep. 10 -8.2%, Ep. 11 +3.3% - so the margin is for noise in either direction.
metadata.purpose: Ep. 12 of the AI in Astronomy & Space Science series, from weekly_stem_videos/ideas.md Astronomy topic 12 (Predicting solar storms - ML models forecasting solar flares that threaten satellites and power grids).
metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity palette. Terracotta #D97757 is the ONE accent and marks THE LEAK AND WHAT IT BUYS - the test rows scattered through every region, the pile of near-zero neighbour distances, the flexible model's inflated bar and its collapse, the inflation curve. Ink marks WHAT SURVIVES AN HONEST TEST - the plain model, which does not move between splits. The mapping never flips, so B05 teaches it once and every later plate reads for free. Accented text is #A44A32; #B9B4A0 is strokes and fills only.
metadata.distinct_from_earlier_episodes: Eps. 01-06 had AI inspecting observations; Ep. 07 standing in for a calculation; Ep. 08 a division of labour; Ep. 09 an output that was never a measurement; Ep. 10 a training set produced by the system's own past decisions; Ep. 11 an objective that omitted the failure. Ep. 12 is the first episode about the EVALUATION rather than the system: the model, the data and the objective can all be fine and the number still be wrong, because of how the test set was built. It is the earliest possible failure - it happens before deployment is even a question, and it is the one that decides whether anything else gets believed.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00, B11, B12, B13. Every other beat illustrates its concept as a reel-local Manim scene (scenes.py). All plates come from assets/gen_solar.py, which runs the experiment described: 350 simulated active regions observed hourly, two models of deliberately different capacity, three splits, 12 repeats, medians throughout. THREE claims are ASSERTED and the script writes nothing if any fails. Seed 1212. PUBLISHED numbers (the 38-of-49 Starlink loss, SWAN-SF's 60:1 imbalance) and COMPUTED-HERE numbers are kept apart on screen and in the voice. The literature supplies the DIAGNOSIS; this reel supplies a MEASUREMENT, and says so - no published paper quantifies the gap. No published figure is reproduced or redrawn. No LaTeX/MathTex anywhere. metadata.channel_title is omitted for the GATE V edge-bleed reason logged in Ep. 03. scenes.py is ASPECT-AWARE, and the two-panel split plate ships in both arrangements (split / split_v) because portrait is not a crop.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about forecasting the solar storms that knock satellites out of orbit, and why the score on the forecast is usually too good to be true.

show.event: the composer types the ask on the cream stage
the send button arms in terracotta
running indicator: splitting 20,228 rows
three result lines land in order

props.command: Machine learning models forecast solar flares from sunspot measurements, and they report strong skill scores. How is that skill measured, and is the number real?
output: every region in the test set was also in training
split it honestly and it drops 75%

beats.narration_text: Eleven episodes of AI in space. This one is about the number we use to decide whether any of it works.

show.event: OM MALI writes in, terracotta hairline underlines it
role line fades in: Humanitarians AI - presenter
a card draws beside it
row one lands and is STRUCK: eleven episodes / does it work
row two lands boxed: this one / how we checked
series line: Ep. 12 - the score was the split

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea. A sunspot region is measured every hour for days. If you shuffle those measurements before splitting them, the model gets tested on regions it already memorised.

show.event: a card draws on the cream stage
line one types: ONE REGION, MEASURED FOR DAYS, sub: dozens of near-identical rows
line two: SHUFFLE, THEN SPLIT, sub: and it lands on both sides
line three lands in the accent and is UNDERLINED: YOU TESTED ITS MEMORY
closer: not its forecast

beats.narration_text: February twenty twenty-two. SpaceX launched forty-nine Starlink satellites into a moderate geomagnetic storm. The air thickened, drag rose, and thirty-eight of them came back down within days. A moderate storm. This is the thing we are trying to forecast.

show.event: a published-ledger chip lands: NASA and Space Weather
forty-nine satellite marks draw in a grid, in ink
a date card: 3 February 2022
thirty-eight of the marks turn terracotta and fall away
a counter lands: 38 of 49
closer: and the storm was only moderate

beats.narration_text: So here is the data. Each row is one active region, measured every hour for days. One region is dozens of rows that barely change. A few regions do all the flaring.

show.event: regions.png fades in: ten tracks of hourly dots
one track is ringed and a counter runs its rows: 1 to 58
the three terracotta rows pulse
a chip lands: 1 flare row in 58
closer: one region, dozens of rows

beats.narration_text: Now split it for testing. Shuffle the rows, and every region lands on both sides, all of them. Split by region instead, and none do.

show.event: split.png: the same tracks twice
left panel - terracotta test rows scatter through every track
a counter lands on the left: 100% of test regions seen in training
right panel - whole tracks go terracotta
the right counter lands: 0%
closer: same data, two answers

beats.narration_text: You can measure the leak directly. For each test row, find the closest row the model trained on. After shuffling, it is nearly always the same region, an hour earlier. Almost the same numbers.

show.event: nearest.png: two distance distributions
the ink distribution is named: split by region
the terracotta pile at near-zero is ringed
a bracket marks the gap, 3x
closer: that is the leak, measured

beats.narration_text: So, two models. A plain one, and a flexible one. Shuffle the rows and the flexible model wins: point four eight against point three six. That is the headline you would publish.

show.event: an empty axis draws, labelled skill score
the ink bar grows to 0.36 - the plain model
the terracotta bar grows past it to 0.48
a bracket marks the gap: +0.13
a chip lands: shuffled rows
closer: the flexible model wins

beats.narration_text: Now split by region. The plain model does not move. The flexible one falls to point one two. Three quarters of its score was the split, not the Sun.

show.event: scores.png: all four bars, the first pair already known
the second ink bar lands at the same height as the first
the second terracotta bar collapses to 0.12
the drop is ringed and a counter runs: -75%
closer: three quarters was the split

beats.narration_text: Twelve runs, same story every time. The plain model sits where it always sat. The flexible one is down here, every single run.

show.event: spread.png: twelve points per column
the two ink columns land, overlapping
the terracotta random-split column lands high
the terracotta by-region column lands far below, no overlap
closer: twelve runs, no overlap

beats.narration_text: And it is the memorising that does it. Strip the region's fingerprint out of the measurements and the gap goes to zero. So the fix is one line: split by region, not by row.

show.event: control.png draws: inflation against fingerprint strength
the curve is followed from right to left
it lands on zero and the zero line is ringed
a card types the fix: split by region, not by row
closer: one line of code

beats.narration_text: So: the model was never the problem. The split was. Ask how the test set was built before you believe any score, including your own.

show.event: the artefact page opens on the cream stage
line one lands
line two lands
line three lands
line four lands
line five lands in the accent

props.artifactTitle: The Same Sunspot, Twice - one page
artifactLines: A sunspot region is measured every hour for days, so one region is dozens of nearly identical rows.
Shuffle the rows before splitting and every region in the test set is also in the training set.
A flexible model then recognises the region instead of forecasting the flare - and scores 0.48 to the simple model's 0.36.
Split by region and it falls to 0.12. Three quarters of its skill was the split.
The fix is one line, and it costs nothing: split by region, not by row.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Read it. Here is how I split my data. Tell me what could appear on both sides, and what my score would look like if I split it properly instead.

show.event: the composer types the handoff prompt
the send button arms
three grading lines land
